items.title: India vs New Zealand - 5th ODI Preview | Surviving the New Ball at Bay Oval
sources: Cricsheet men's ODI ball-by-ball archive (cricsheet.org/downloads/odis_json.zip, ODC-BY), 50-over matches 2002 to 25 Oct 2025 (2,617 matches, 5,165 innings; super overs excluded). Coverage is partial (no matches before 2002, thin in the early 2000s), so 'archive' figures are samples, not complete records. Bay Oval = the 13 men's ODIs at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui; 'new ball' = overs 1-10; wickets include run outs, exclude retired hurt; chases exclude D/L results. Figures: analysis/bay_oval_new_ball.py and make_bay_oval_preview.py.

ESPNcricinfo match capture, NZ v IND 4th ODI, Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui (match 1539440): ball-by-ball with line, length, shot and control, captured with our own tool; first-ten-over figures computed from it.

Cricbuzz match capture (match 161271): over-by-over cross-check; match notes (toss, conditions, dropped catches) used as leads. Result in both: New Zealand won by 244 runs; Player of the Match Matt Henry.
Bay Oval's 13 earlier men's ODIs were reconciled against ESPNcricinfo's ground results list (all dates, winners and margins match); the 14th is the 4th ODI capture.

Series position (India 2-1; third ODI rained off) and the 5th ODI date (15 Nov) from ESPN's fixture list and the channel's schedule; squads, toss, weather and pitch for the 5th ODI were not yet confirmed when this was made.

First-over records: Chaminda Vaas, 4 wickets in his first over (Bangladesh v Sri Lanka, 2003 World Cup) and Shaun Pollock, 3 in his first over (South Africa v Pakistan, Lahore, 1990s): ESPNcricinfo records and Sportskeeda; Henry's figures (3 wickets, 0 runs, first over) from our captures.

items.title: Fielding Positions Explained: How to Read Any Field | Did You Know Ep 2
sources: Names and definitions, checked against two independent written sources: Wikipedia, 'Fielding (cricket)' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_(cricket) (names as an angle word plus a distance word; silly, short, deep, long; square; slips numbered outwards from the wicket-keeper; positions 'neither fixed nor precisely defined') and 'Glossary of cricket terms' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cricket_terms (cover, fine, cordon); and SportPlan, 'Cricket Fielding Positions Explained' https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Cricket/guides/cricket-fielding-positions-explained.jsp (sides, square, slips, gully, third man, mirrored for left-handers).

Law 28.4 (Limitation of on side fielders): MCC Laws of Cricket, 2017 Code (3rd edition 2022), Law 28 'The Fielder' https://www.lords.org/mcc/the-laws/the-fielder (also quoted by Wisden, https://www.wisden.com/series/australia-in-england-2024/cricket-news/england-concede-rare-bodyline-no-ball-for-illegal-leg-side-field-placings); ICC Men's Test Playing Conditions clause 28.4 https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/mens-test-match-clause-28-the-fielder and Men's ODI clause 28.4.2-28.4.3 (striker's end umpire calls no ball) https://icc-cricket.com/news/mens-odi-match-clause-28-the-fielder. The 'on side' is the leg side for the batter.

MCC published a 2026 edition of the Laws, in force from October 2026 (https://www.lords.org/getmedia/72990a68-98cd-4c6e-89ac-a2dce54533ad/Ten-major-changes-to-Laws-for-2026-edition_5.pdf); its ten headline changes do not touch Law 28, but the full 2026 text was not read, so check the clause number against the current edition. Field plans are illustrative, for a right-handed batter (mirrored for a left-hander). Figures: make_dyk_fielding.py.

items.title: Third Man Explained: Position, Purpose and the Name Mystery | Did You Know Ep 1
sources: Position and job: Wikipedia, 'Glossary of cricket terms' (third man: behind the wicket-keeper on the off side, beyond the slip and gully areas) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cricket_terms and 'Fielding (cricket)' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_(cricket); SportPlan, 'Cricket Fielding Positions Explained' https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Cricket/guides/cricket-fielding-positions-explained.jsp; cricketwriter.com, 'Third Man' https://www.cricketwriter.com/cricket-fielding-positions-third-man/.
Who stands there: Wikipedia 'Fielding (cricket)' and PitchVision, 'Specialist fielding: fine leg and third man' https://cdn0.pitchvision.com/specialist-fielding-fine-leg-and-third-man.

The four theories are repeated on cricket websites (Cricket Lounge https://thecricketlounge.com/read-the-story-behind-the-third-man-position-in-cricket/ ; Idiom Origins https://idiomorigins.org/origin/third-man ; cricketwriter.com; the History of Cricket blog); none cites a source. We found no document that settles the origin; the video shows each as unproven.

The 1884 text: James Lillywhite's Cricketers' Companion 1884, 'Diagrams of the Field', ACS online library https://archive.acscricket.com/online_library/jlcc/lillywhite_companion_1884/55/ : "It is the fashion now ... to dispense with long-stop, thereby getting a 'third man' as well as 'mid-on'". The earliest mention we found, not necessarily the earliest.

India v Pakistan, ICC World Cup, SuperSport Park, Centurion, 1 March 2003: Cricsheet ball-by-ball (Tendulkar 98 off 75 balls, first six off Shoaib Akhtar in the second over; India 276/4 chasing Pakistan's 273/7, won by six wickets) and Wikipedia, 'India at the Cricket World Cup'. The shot's direction (an upper cut over third man) is as reported by ESPNcricinfo and Sportskeeda. Field plans are illustrative: right-handed batter, bowler at the top.

Check (14 Nov 2026): Kohli's six T20 World Cup knockout innings 72*, 77, 89*, 50, 9, 76 = 373 runs, 4 dismissals, average 93.25. The earlier 'best of any batter' claim was removed: it came from a partial Cricsheet archive and was not checked against complete records.

items.title: Virat Kohli: Is He Too Slow for T20? | Myth or Data Ep 2
sources: Sportmonks ball-by-ball, IPL 2013-2026 (data/ipl cache). Virat Kohli's legal balls faced; super overs excluded; strike rate = runs off the bat per 100 balls; powerplay = overs 1-6; bowler type from Sportmonks bowling style. League strike rate = all batters' runs off the bat per 100 legal balls in the season. Figures: make_kohli_reinvention.py.

Cross-check: Kohli's 2026 total (675 runs, strike rate about 165.8) matches RCB's own season review: https://royalchallengers.com/rcb-cricket-news/news/from-virat-kohli-to-tim-david-rcbs-top-five-batters-in-ipl-2026

items.title: Aaryavir Sehwag: Like Father, Like Son? | Myth or Data Ep 3
sources: Aaryavir Sehwag's five innings: the Cricbuzz commentary captures of the Nepal (4th match), Pakistan (8th match), UAE (11th match) and Afghanistan (semi-final) games, and the final (Cricbuzz 175720 + Cricinfo 1558444). His totals (361 runs, average 90.25, one hundred, three fifties) reproduce the Player of the Tournament figures in BCCI's Instagram post.

Quote: Aaryavir Sehwag to the media after his 160 vs UAE, as reported by Outlook India: https://www.outlookindia.com/sports/cricket/india-vs-uae-u-19-asia-cup-2026-aaryavir-sehwag-promise-father-virender

Earlier big scores (press reports): 297 in the Cooch Behar Trophy https://cricket.com/news/virender-sehwags-son-aaryavir-smashes-297-in-cooch-behar-trophy-11222024-1732257974695 ; 173 off 143 in the Vinoo Mankad Trophy https://www.bjsports.live/latest-news-en/aaryavir-sehwag-smashes-173-off-143-to-lead-delhi-u19-in-vinoo-mankad-trophy ; 160 off 168 vs UAE https://wisden.com/cricket-news/son-of-india-legend-aaryavir-sehwag-smashes-160-in-168-balls-for-india-u19

Virender Sehwag's career figures: ESPNcricinfo player profile and Wikipedia (Tests: 8,586 runs, 23 hundreds, 32 fifties, highest 319; ODIs: 251 matches, 8,273 runs, 15 hundreds, 38 fifties, strike rate 104.33, 1,132 fours, 136 sixes). Checked 14 Nov 2026.

Style comparison for Virender Sehwag: Cricsheet ball-by-ball archive (cricsheet.org, ODC-BY), 165 of his ODI innings 2002-2013 (a sample: coverage is partial), balls faced exclude wides. The two players' figures come from different levels of cricket (Under-19 against senior internationals), so they show style, not quality.
All figures computed in make_aaryavir.py. Graphics are original illustrations: no photographs or likeness of any player.

items.title: India vs New Zealand - 4th ODI Analysis | How 333 Became 89 (Every Ball)
sources: ESPNcricinfo match capture, NZ v IND 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui (match 1539440): ball-by-ball with line, length, shot, control and wagon data, captured with our own tool.

items.title: India vs New Zealand - 5th ODI Analysis | How India Won at 22%
sources: Ball-by-ball: Cricbuzz full-commentary capture of the 5th ODI (match 161282), parsed into one row per delivery (data/series/nz_ind_2026); innings totals and individual figures checked against Wikipedia's match box ('Indian cricket team in New Zealand in 2026-27', citing Cricinfo) and Cricbuzz's own pace/spin summary line.

Win probability, swings, 'win probability added' and the hidden winner: our own model, fitted on 1,719 men's 50-over ODIs in the Cricsheet archive (2009 onwards, no rain method), validated on held-out matches (accuracy 83%); an indication, not a fact. Drops: the runs a batter scored after a dropped chance (descriptive, not a counterfactual).
4th ODI comparison: Cricbuzz capture of the 4th ODI, with an independent Cricinfo capture agreeing over by over. Figures: analysis/nz_ind_*.py, make_replay_5odi.py.

items.title: India vs Pakistan - U19 Asia Cup Final Analysis | 338 Chased Off the Last Ball
sources: ESPNcricinfo match capture, India U19 v Pakistan U19, ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026 final, Al Amerat, Oman, 14 Nov 2026 (match 1558444): ball-by-ball with line, length, shot and control, captured with our own tool.

Cricbuzz match capture (match 175720): over-by-over cross-check (all runs match) and the first-innings scorecard (Pakistan's batting and India's bowling figures agree with our figures). Result in both: India won by 1 wicket (0 balls remaining).

Tournament path (group and semi-final results) from the Cricinfo series standings in the same capture. Conventions: balls faced exclude wides; bowler runs exclude byes and leg byes; a run out is not credited to the bowler.

All figures computed in make_u19_final.py and analysis/u19_final.py from data/cricinfo/u19_final_balls.csv. Web coverage of this match was not yet indexed when this was made, so no record claims are made. Graphics are original illustrations, not broadcast footage.
